contribution: Methods for the empirical analysis of markets with differentiated products and imperfect competition, enabling estimation of demand, market power and the effects of mergers and policy
rationale: This is a speculative guess. Recent prizes went to institutions and growth (2024–2025), so a turn toward microeconomic methods is plausible. Empirical industrial organization, especially the Berry–Levinsohn–Pakes demand framework, is widely used in antitrust and academia and has long appeared on shortlists. Other contenders include Richard Blundell, Michael Woodford and Jordi Galí, and public-finance figures such as Emmanuel Saez.
